fields.title: Nothing checks that a skipped test cites a deviation

sections.What it checks:
* [std-GATES.BLOCK](https://github.com/paul80nd/knowledge-as-code/blob/01c2db7153b064d26441c61b1aa8dd22e4dac7f7/examples/engineering/standards/common/build-gates.md#block-a-failing-check-stops-the-change) says a team "**MUST NOT** skip, silence or suppress a check without a
  recorded deviation".
sections.How it works:
Nothing runs. The check this rule needs is a pipeline job over the lines a pull request adds. It fails on a line that adds a skip marker and cites no deviation id:

```sh
git diff -U0 origin/main...HEAD \
  | grep -E '^\+.*(Skip *=|\[Ignore|mark\.skip|pytest\.skip\(|t\.Skip\(|(it|test)\.skip\()' \
  | grep -vE 'dev-[a-z0-9-]+'
```

The job fails where that prints a line. The same pattern can run over the staged diff as a pre-commit check, or over the written content as a Claude Code hook on `Write` and `Edit`.
sections.Coverage and gaps:
A reviewer reading the test diff is the only thing that notices an uncited skip today.

The check proves an id is cited. It cannot tell whether the deviation exists, names an owner, or is inside its review date, which the other rules under [std-GATES.BLOCK](https://github.com/paul80nd/knowledge-as-code/blob/01c2db7153b064d26441c61b1aa8dd22e4dac7f7/examples/engineering/standards/common/build-gates.md#block-a-failing-check-stops-the-change) require. It knows only the markers in its pattern, so a skip in another framework, or a pipeline step set to continue on error, passes it. The rule lets a test be guarded off a platform it cannot run on without a deviation, and the check fails such a guard where it uses one of the markers. A reviewer decides whether a required check runs the test on a platform where it can.
